title: QA run · walled:isolated+group (11/14) · 580fd4ed · 2026-10-20 · 8 PASS / 1 PARTIAL / 1 FAIL / 1 BLOCKED / 3 NOT-RUN
body:
QA run record: the walled-posture pass of the 18.0 round-3 top-up (anchor #24579). Server half (2): `surface:cli`, `surface:build` and this walled pass. The sister card S1 runs `surface:api` on the default `single` posture and parked its walled legs here. Maintainer-approved top-up, dispatched from session `session_01CfRDy7SuTfUqaTu2AEH2Hi` on 2026-10-20.

Scope rule for this record: for each item, only the walled leg is judged, i.e. the clauses its `fixtures.knownGaps` names as walled. Each is judged once under `isolated` and once under `group`, and both answers are written. Non-walled clauses are `out of scope (walled pass)`. Console clauses are `not-run (browser)`. A knownGaps entry recorded as blocked for another reason is carried as written.

## Environment fingerprint

- framework: `580fd4ed3c98a1752dfb0041b45cc713644fef7e` (no pull, no sha change). `.objectui-sha`: not used. The console was not built, by dispatch decision.
- build: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` then `pnpm build --concurrency=2`, giving 76/76 tasks. `node scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs` is green.
- runner: one Claude Code cloud session. A second, independent agent did the RUNNER rule 7 re-derivation (see "Rule 7").
- scratch app: a copy of `examples/app-showcase` (tar, without `node_modules`, `.objectstack` or `dist`) in a session scratch directory. Its own `package.json` carries every showcase dependency as `link:` to the workspace package, plus `"@objectstack/organizations": "link:/home/user/objectstack/packages/plugins/organizations"`, installed there with `pnpm install --ignore-workspace`.
  - Package-file refs, for example the OpenAPI connector spec, resolve against the served root, so a config that only re-exports the stock showcase does not boot. The copy has to carry `src/`.
- boot command, run from the scratch app:
  - `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL=admin@objectos.ai OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY=invite-only OS_PORT=P OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated|group node packages/cli/bin/run.js dev --seed-admin -p P -d file:RUNDIR/{iso,grp}.db`
  - `isolated` ran on port 47621, then `group` on 47631, one after the other.
  - A third short `isolated` boot on 47651 ran the removed-member producer probe.
  - Each boot printed `Tenancy: isolated` or `Tenancy: group` and mounted `Organizations`. `GET /api/v1/auth/config` answered `features.multiOrgEnabled: true` with `tenancyPosture` equal to the posture.
- personas, per boot:
  - operator `admin@objectos.ai`: the seeded admin. It is `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, positions include `platform_admin`, and `isPlatformAdmin: true`.
  - A, B, N: minted with `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user`, then `change-password`. Self-registration answers `403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED` (audience `invite_only`). Each answered `membershipCreated: false`.
  - A and B each created their own organization: `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/create`, then `set-active`.
  - N holds no membership at all.
  - A later created a second organization, A2.
- fixture writes made outside HTTP (system-level stamps on the run's own scratch SQLite, never a shared DB):
  - one `sys_user_permission_set` row granting A a runtime-authored `qa_meta_author` set (`systemPermissions: ['manage_metadata']`) in organization A. No HTTP door could place it: the operator is refused writing into an organization it is not a member of, and A's own org-admin insert is refused by ADR-0090 D12 condition (c).
  - `sys_setting.locked = 1` on A's tenant row. No HTTP door sets a tenant lock: `sys_setting` refuses `update` with 405 `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, and `PUT /api/settings/NS` carries no lock.
  - one legacy unscoped `admin_full_access` grant row for N, used for the platform-owner leg.
- times (UTC): install and build 04:57–05:09. Scratch app and prerequisite probes 05:10–05:17. `isolated` 05:17–05:26, `group` 05:26–05:30, removed-member probe 05:37–05:39.

### Environment self-check (run before scoring)

- `OS_TEST_TIERS=nightly` vitest `packages/cli/test/serve-organizations-host-resolution.e2e.test.ts` and `serve-organizations-mount-failure.e2e.test.ts`: Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 7 passed (7). These are the seven walled e2e cases.
- vitest `packages/qa/dogfood/test/wall-*.dogfood.test.ts`: Test Files 6 passed (6), Tests 121 passed (121).
- Prerequisite refusals, measured through `os dev` from the scratch app under `isolated`, one prerequisite absent each time:
  - `@objectstack/organizations` removed from the app's `package.json` (the link still present in `node_modules`): exit 1, `✖ FATAL: tenancy posture 'isolated' was requested but @objectstack/organizations could not be loaded, so the organization wall is INACTIVE … (ADR-0093 D5)`.
  - `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` unset: exit 1, `✗ [auth] tenancy posture 'isolated' requires OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL to be set …`.
  - `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY` unset: exit 1, `✖ FATAL: tenancy posture 'isolated' is walled, but this deployment never declared a membership policy` (membership policy "auto", source: default).
  - With all three present, the boot served (`✓ Server is ready`, health 200). No FATAL refusal occurred with the prerequisites met.

## Scope: items and revisions

`access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics` r4 (P0) · `access-security.walled-environment-metadata-operator-only` r3 (P0) · `platform-core.settings-organization-isolation-and-platform-rung` r3 · `access-security.activation-write-operator-gate` r6 · `access-security.platform-owner-email-anchor` r5 · `access-security.grant-table-write-contract` r4 · `access-security.parent-and-organization-write-guards` r3 · `records-forms.record-discussion-mentions` r4 · `integration-system.webhook-lifecycle` r8 (all P1) · `api-backend.action-activation-door-contract` r3 · `attachments-storage.chunked-upload-integrity` r5 · `automation.connector-dispatch-matrix` r3 · `identity-auth.workspace-org-switch` r4 · `studio-authoring.metadata-diagnostics-sweep` r5 (all P2).

## Per-clause verdicts (walled legs only; ISO = isolated, GRP = group)

### access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics (P0): FAIL (GRP), pass on ISO

The whole item is a walled leg (requires[0]). Producer used: walled posture plus `invite-only`. An admin-created user with no membership is durable and non-racy: ADR-0093 D1 `no-target-org`, `membershipCreated: false`. Its session reads `activeOrganizationId: null` (get-session payload) and it has 0 `sys_member` rows. Second producer: an organization member who clears the active org with `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/set-active {"organizationId": null}`; get-session then reads null.

- a[0] tenant-scoped reads resolve to nothing:
  - ISO pass: N, `GET /data/showcase_task` and `/data/showcase_account` answer 200 `records: []`.
  - GRP pass for N.
  - Note: under GRP the member with no active org (A) reads its own organization's rows (11 tasks, all organization A), because group reads span the caller's memberships. See accuracy finding F3.
- a[1] tenant-scoped writes refused 4xx naming the missing org:
  - ISO pass: N and A (cleared) get `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` "[Security] Access denied: 'showcase_task' is scoped to an organization, and this session has no active organization — so this insert has no organization to place the record in …".
  - GRP pass for N, same 403.
  - GRP **fail** for A (member, cleared active org): `POST /api/v1/data/showcase_task` answers `500 {"error":"Internal server error","code":"ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED"}`. Reproduced twice by the runner and twice by the rule-7 verifier on fresh boots. Reproduction is below.
  - `showcase_account` is no control: its 403 is the object-permission gate (`allowCreate: false` for the caller's sets), which runs first.
- a[2] no NULL stamping: ISO pass, GRP pass. Admin-side counts of `showcase_task` / `showcase_account` rows with NULL or empty `organization_id` were 0 before and 0 after every refused attempt, including the 500s, and no row titled with the probe exists.
- a[3] org-scoped holder with no active org reads and writes nothing across tenants:
  - ISO pass: A (owner of org A, `organization_admin` in A) with active org cleared. `/auth/me/permissions` drops `organization_admin`, so `systemPermissions` is []. Lists of `showcase_task`, `showcase_account`, `sys_member` and `sys_invitation` return 0 rows. B's task by id answers 404, and so does A's own task. Writes are refused, and `invite-member` into B's org answers `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`.
  - GRP pass on the cross-tenant point: A sees only organization A rows (its membership), and B's task answers 404.
- a[4] audit rows are not permanently invisible:
  - ISO and GRP pass, with a note. N's `login`/`logout` rows in `sys_audit_log` carry `tenant_id: null` because the user belongs to no organization at all, so there is no real tenant to stamp.
  - The platform operator reads them through `GET /api/v1/data/sys_audit_log?filter={user_id}` (200, login and logout listed), so they are not invisible to every RLS reader. N itself gets 403 on `sys_audit_log`. See F3.
- a[5] the state is legal and nothing 500s:
  - ISO pass: get-session 200, `GET /data/sys_user` 200, `POST /auth/update-user` 200, no 5xx.
  - GRP **fail**: the member write path in a[1] answers 500 (negative[3]).
- a[6] the three subsystems agree:
  - ISO pass. Sharing drops org grants with no active org; the wall gives empty reads and 403 writes; the audit rows are recorded and readable by the operator.
  - GRP **fail**: the write path gives two answers to the same state, 403 for a non-member and 500 for a member.
- Negatives: negative[0], [1], [2], [4] and [5] did not occur on either posture. negative[3] (a 500) occurred on GRP.

### access-security.walled-environment-metadata-operator-only (P0): PASS

The walled legs per knownGaps[0] are a[1], a[2] and negative[0]. A holds `manage_metadata` in organization A only: `/auth/me/permissions` includes it, positions are `[org_owner, everyone]`, `isPlatformAdmin: false`.

- a[1]: ISO pass, GRP pass. As A:
  - `PUT /meta/object/qa_walled_probe` (sharingModel set) → 403 FORBIDDEN, "… requires the platform operator: this deployment runs the 'isolated'/'group' tenancy posture …".
  - `PUT /meta/permission/showcase_member_access` → 403 FORBIDDEN.
  - `POST /meta/view/showcase_task.urgent/publish` → 403 FORBIDDEN.
  - `DELETE /packages/com.example.showcase` → 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
  - `POST /security/permission-sets/showcase_member_default/clone` → 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
  - `POST /meta/_migrate-stored` → 403 FORBIDDEN.
  - `POST /automation` → 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
  - `POST /marketplace/install-local` with a catalog-carrying manifest → 403 FORBIDDEN.
  - Read-backs as the operator: the object, clone and flow answer 404, the package is absent, and the showcase package is still present.
- a[2], walled half: ISO pass, GRP pass. The operator's identical object PUT answers 200 ("Saved object … env-wide"), GET answers 200, and the follow-up delete answers 200. The `single` half is out of scope (walled pass).
- negative[0]: ISO pass, GRP pass. No org-owner write succeeded.

### platform-core.settings-organization-isolation-and-platform-rung (P1): PASS

- a[2]: ISO pass, GRP pass.
  - A `PUT /api/settings/company {"legal_name":"A Corp"}` stores a tenant row in organization A. B's read stays default/null, then B's own value. The lock was stamped on A's row (see the fixture writes above); A's read shows `locked: true`.
  - B reads `locked: false` and B's write is admitted. The DB holds one row per organization, A locked and B unlocked.
- a[3]: ISO pass, GRP pass. The operator with active org cleared, `PUT /api/settings/company` → `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` "… Legal name is a per-organization setting, and this write names no organization to store it for …". No row was written.
  - Callers without `setup.write` get `403 SETTINGS_FORBIDDEN` first.

### access-security.activation-write-operator-gate (P1): PASS

The walled leg is a[4], live.

- ISO pass, GRP pass. As A (org admin with `manage_metadata`):
  - `POST /automation/showcase_urgent_task_alert/toggle {"enabled":false}` → 403 PERMISSION_DENIED "Enabling or disabling a packaged flow writes an INSTALL-WIDE activation row, and this deployment runs the 'isolated'/'group' tenancy posture … It requires the platform operator (ADR-0126 §5) … ask your platform operator; an organization that needs flows of its own is given an environment of its own." No clone is recommended.
  - Action door `POST /actions/_activation/showcase_task/showcase_mark_done` → the 403 action sentence, also operator-only with no clone.
  - The invalid body `{"enabled":"false"}` still answers the 403.
  - `sys_metadata_activation` is empty after the refusals.
- The operator's toggles answer 200 at both doors. The ledger rows are `flow` and `action`, `active: false`, with no `organization_id` key on either. Both were restored to enabled.
- B (no `manage_metadata`) gets the tier sentence "requires the `manage_metadata` capability".

### access-security.platform-owner-email-anchor (P1): PASS

The walled half of a[5], live.

- ISO pass, GRP pass. The config anchor confers on the walled rig: the operator has `isPlatformAdmin: true` and `platform_admin` among its positions.
- A legacy unscoped `admin_full_access` grant row (N, `organization_id` NULL) confers no rung on a walled posture: N reads positions `[everyone]`, `isPlatformAdmin: false`. The held set's capabilities still apply: `GET /datasources` answers 200 and `systemPermissions` includes `manage_platform_settings`. This matches the clause ("the held set still grants its own capabilities; only the rung and the built-in platform_admin position go").
- With that set, N is still refused metadata writes: 403 "requires the platform operator".

### access-security.grant-table-write-contract (P1): PASS

- a[4]: ISO pass, GRP pass. A (org admin, org A) `POST /data/sys_user_permission_set {"user_id": B, "permission_set": "showcase_member_default"}` → 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, `fields[0] {field: user_id, code: reference_not_found}`, "… is not a member of the organization … add the user to that organization first".
- Controls: naming B's organization explicitly → 403 "the row belongs to organization …, not the one you administer". A grant to A itself → 201.

### access-security.parent-and-organization-write-guards (P1): PASS

- a[1]: ISO pass, GRP pass.
  - A `PATCH /data/showcase_task/ID {"organization_id": null}` → 403 PERMISSION_DENIED "the update would leave 'showcase_task' with no organization". `""` gives the same answer. Naming B's org → 403 "would place … in another tenant". The row is unchanged.
  - Inserts carrying `organization_id: ""` or `null` → 201, stamped with organization A (DB read).

### records-forms.record-discussion-mentions (P1): NOT-RUN (no walled leg)

- Its knownGaps names no walled leg. The hit that put it on the list is a pin fixture name (`lead_walled`); see F1. Every clause is out of scope (walled pass), and the console clauses are not-run (browser).
- Observed while probing the server half on both walled boots: an authorization / tenancy-wall finding, filed separately with detail withheld pending maintainer (see "Extracted"). Reproduced on both postures by the runner and by the rule-7 verifier.

### integration-system.webhook-lifecycle (P1): BLOCKED

- a[2] (bulk pair): `blocked(dependency)`, carried as knownGaps[1] writes it. The flow-node predicate multi-write organization question on #23166 is unruled. Not hard-judged.
- Observed on both walled boots, outside the clauses:
  - The declared `showcase_task_changed` is switched on only by the operator. An org admin gets 403 "writes an INSTALL-WIDE activation row … requires the platform operator"; an undeclared name answers 404.
  - Once on, it delivered one `sys_http_delivery` row per task create, stamped with that event's organization: `declared:showcase_task_changed` for A, and the same for B. Each organization reads only its own delivery rows.
  - An in-organization scratch `sys_webhook` authored by A (organization A) received A's create only. B's create in the same window did not reach it. B reads no `sys_webhook` row of A's: list empty, by-id 404, PATCH 404.
  - B's `POST /api/v1/webhooks/redeliver` of A's delivery id → 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.
  - See F4: requires[0]'s "under a walled posture it would be refused as belonging to no organization" no longer holds.

### api-backend.action-activation-door-contract (P2): PASS

The walled reading is a[0], authority first under a wall. knownGaps[2] calls it unreachable; see F5.

- ISO pass, GRP pass.
  - A (org admin with `manage_metadata`) `POST /actions/_activation/showcase_task/no_such_action {"enable": false}` (mis-bodied and undeclared) → 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with the posture/operator sentence. That is neither the 400 nor the 404, and it recommends no clone.
  - B (no `manage_metadata`) → 403 with the `manage_metadata` "functionally equivalent to deleting it" sentence. Anonymous → 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.
- Operator controls: undeclared → 404 "has no declaration — there is nothing to switch off"; `{"enable":false}` on the declared action → 400 VALIDATION_FAILED `unknown_field`, "did you mean `enabled`?".
- No ledger row was written by any refusal.

### attachments-storage.chunked-upload-integrity (P2): PASS

- a[3]: ISO pass, GRP pass.
  - Cookie sign-in as A with active org A. `POST /api/v1/storage/upload/chunked` (2 chunks), then chunk 0 → 200.
  - `set-active` to A2, then chunk 1 PUT → `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` "This upload was started in a different organization than your active one …", and complete → the same 409.
  - Progress → 200, `status: in_progress`, `uploadedChunks: 1`. Its `expiresAt` is 24 h after the start, so the stamp is not due.
- Cross-user probe: B with A's upload id gets progress 403 "Only the user who started this upload can act on it" and file URL 404.

### automation.connector-dispatch-matrix (P2): NOT-RUN (no walled leg)

- No walled leg: the "isolated boot" in its text means the dogfood §0 own-port boot (F1).
- Observed: on both walled boots a task created in organization A or B fired `showcase_declarative_connector_ping` and `showcase_mcp_connector_echo`, both `completed`, with runs stamped with that organization. Each organization reads only its own `sys_automation_run` rows.

### identity-auth.workspace-org-switch (P2): PARTIAL

- a[0], a[2], a[4]: not-run (browser). The posture precheck for a[0] holds: `/auth/config` `tenancyPosture` is isolated/group and `multiOrgEnabled: true`.
- a[1]: ISO pass, GRP pass. A, holding organizations A and A2, `set-active` A2 → 200. `get-active-member` names A2.
- a[3]: ISO pass, GRP pass.
  - ISO: A's org-A task by id → 404 after the switch, and the list holds only A2 rows (10 seeded).
  - GRP: org-A rows stay readable (13 A plus 10 A2, reads span memberships), and a create after the switch lands in A2 (DB read of `organization_id`).
  - Both: `GET /meta/object/showcase_task` is byte-identical (md5) before and after.
- a[5] API half: ISO pass, GRP pass. Forged `set-active` to B's organization → `403 USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THE_ORGANIZATION`. Afterwards `get-active-member` → `400 NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` and get-session active is null, never B's org. The UI half is not-run (browser).

### studio-authoring.metadata-diagnostics-sweep (P2): NOT-RUN (no walled leg)

- No walled leg: "isolated scratch file DB" means the run's own DB (F1).
- Observed on both walled boots: an org admin `GET /meta/diagnostics` → 200 `entries: []`, `scannedTypes: 28`, `scannedItems: 402`. `?type=viewes` → 400 with the spelling refusal.

## Reproduction rule: the one publishable fail (GRP only)

1. Boot the scratch app as in the fingerprint, with `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=group`.
2. As the operator, `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user {"email":"qa-a@wall.test","password":"…"}`. Sign in as that user, change the password, and sign in again to get token T.
3. `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/create {"name":"qa-org-a","slug":"qa-org-a"}`, then `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/set-active {"organizationId": "ORG_A"}`.
4. Create `showcase_account {name}`, then `showcase_project {name, account}`, and keep the project id.
5. `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/set-active {"organizationId": null}`. `GET /api/v1/auth/get-session` now shows `session.activeOrganizationId: null`.
6. `POST /api/v1/data/showcase_task {"title":"x","project":"PROJECT_ID"}`.
   - expected (a[1], and the ISO answer to the same steps): 403 PERMISSION_DENIED naming the missing active organization.
   - actual: `500 {"error":"Internal server error","code":"ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED"}`. The server log shows `[REST] Unhandled error: SystemWriteOrganizationRequiredError: Insert on 'showcase_task' was REFUSED: a system-context write on a tenant-scoped object must carry an organization …`. No row was written.
- Disposition: product defect. The fix is in the walled write path, not the checklist; it was extracted.

## Rule 7

The P0 `fail` and the authorization finding were re-derived by an independent agent on its own fresh `isolated` and `group` boots, from the steps alone. It agrees on both:
- the 500 reproduces on `group` only, with no row written;
- the 403 holds for a member-less caller on both postures;
- the 500 is error-contract severity, not a security bypass: the write is evaluated as the session, and only the error text says "system-context".

## Removed-member producer (knownGaps[0] of the P0 item)

On `isolated`:
1. The operator `add-member`s M into organization A. M's session reads A's task (200).
2. A `remove-member`s M; M's `sys_member` count is 0.
3. M's live token then answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED on reads, list, create and update. The removal revokes the session, so this path no longer yields "a live session with no organization" (F3).

## Extracted

See the comments below; card numbers are added at close-out.

## Checklist-accuracy findings / fixture gaps (for the anchor #24579, not extracted)

- F1, the dispatch's list of 14 walled items: three carry no walled leg in `fixtures.knownGaps`. Their keyword hit is a word collision:
  - `records-forms.record-discussion-mentions`: the pin fixture name `lead_walled`.
  - `automation.connector-dispatch-matrix`: "boot showcase isolated", the dogfood §0 own-port boot.
  - `studio-authoring.metadata-diagnostics-sweep`: "isolated scratch file DB".
  - They are NOT-RUN here, so the denominator 14 overstates the walled set by three.
- F2, the RUNNER entry "A walled boot is a fixture of its own" and the rewritten knownGaps:
  - The three prerequisites refuse as described through `os dev`.
  - Through bare `os serve` (and so `os start`) without `NODE_ENV=development`, the boot runs in production mode and needs `OS_AUTH_SECRET` and a stable encryption key first. Without them `AuthPlugin` is skipped (`⚠ AuthPlugin skipped — set OS_AUTH_SECRET …`), the walled `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` and membership-policy gates never run, and the walled server comes up `⚠ Server is ready — DEGRADED: missing core services: auth`, not FATAL. Measured with `os serve --no-ui` from the scratch app, prerequisites 1 and 3 present and 2 absent, and with 1 and 2 present and 3 absent.
  - So the entry's "each one absent refuses the boot naming itself" holds for `os dev` only; `serve`/`start` need the auth secret as a fourth prerequisite before the other two are judged.
  - A config that only re-exports `examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts` from a scratch directory does not boot: package-file refs (the OpenAPI connector spec) resolve against the served root. The scratch app must be a full copy.
- F3, `access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics`:
  - knownGaps[0] and [1] say the durable producers are the removed-member path or a reconciler that binds nobody, and that `invite-only` is blocked(fixture). On a walled boot with `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY=invite-only` (a walled-boot prerequisite), every admin-created user lands with `membershipCreated: false`, which is a durable producer. `set-active {"organizationId": null}` is a second durable producer.
  - The removed-member path now revokes the session (401), so it no longer produces the state.
  - a[0] reads "resolve to nothing", but under `group` a member with no active org reads its memberships' rows by design. The clause should scope itself to a caller with no membership, or say what `group` answers.
  - a[4] assumes every first-session audit row has a real tenant; for a user with no organization at all the rows are NULL-tenanted and readable only by the platform operator. The clause should say whether that is the intended answer.
- F4, `integration-system.webhook-lifecycle` requires[0]: "under a walled posture it would be refused as belonging to no organization" is stale.
  - Under `isolated` and `group` the declared webhook, switched on by the operator, delivers one row per event stamped with that event's organization, and each organization reads only its own. That is the shape `wall-declared-webhook-deployment-wide.dogfood.test.ts` pins.
  - Creating a scratch `sys_webhook` over `/data` needs `definition_json` (required) and lower-case `method`; the recipe names neither.
- F5, `api-backend.action-activation-door-contract` knownGaps[2] still says the group/isolated legs "need an enterprise tenancy runtime no example app composes". That is stale since #24580; a scratch app with the open `@objectstack/organizations` composes it, and the ordering held on both postures.
- F6, `platform-core.settings-organization-isolation-and-platform-rung` steps[2] says "save a tenant key and lock it". No HTTP door sets a tenant-row lock: `sys_setting` refuses update 405, and the settings PUT carries no lock. The run stamped `locked` directly, so the step needs a named recipe.
- F7, `access-security.walled-environment-metadata-operator-only` requires[2] and `access-security.activation-write-operator-gate` need an organization owner holding `manage_metadata` in their own org. No HTTP door grants it on a walled boot:
  - the operator cannot insert a grant into an organization it is not a member of (403 "outside the caller's organization scope");
  - the org admin's own insert is refused (ADR-0090 D12 condition (c): `manage_metadata` is not scope `org`).
  - The run used a system stamp; the fixture needs a named recipe (the dogfood harness inserts it through the engine).
- F8, `identity-auth.workspace-org-switch` requires[0]: the parenthetical "measured by QA run #23166 … REFUSES TO BOOT" predates #24580, and step text should cite the RUNNER walled-boot entry instead. A user can hold two memberships by creating a second organization itself; the platform-admin `add-member` is not needed.

## Handover

None of the 14 is left un-handled. The three NOT-RUN items have no walled leg (F1). The browser clauses of `identity-auth.workspace-org-switch` need a console build.
